classification.difficultyReason: Model eight end-of-year deposits as a geometric series, calculate the future value and compare it with the trip cost.

content.prompt:
Prim is saving up to go overseas in 8 years’ time. She invests $\$1000$ at the end of each year at 7% p.a. and estimates that the trip will cost her around $\$10\,000$. Will she have enough?

If so, how much over will it be? If she doesn’t have enough, how much will she need to add to this money to make it up to the $\$10\,000$? Give monetary answers to the nearest cent.

answer.short: Yes. She will have $\$10\,259.80$, which is $\$259.80$ over the estimated cost.
answer.worked:
End of 1st year: $1000$

End of 2nd year: $1000(1.07)+1000$

End of 8th year: $1000(1.07)^7+1000(1.07)^6+\cdots+1000$

This is a geometric series with $a=1000$, common ratio $R=1.07$ and $n=8$.

$$\begin{aligned}FV&=\frac{1000(1.07^8-1)}{1.07-1}\\&\approx\$10\,259.80\end{aligned}$$

Amount over $\$10\,000$:

$$\begin{aligned}\text{Surplus}&=\frac{1000(1.07^8-1)}{1.07-1}-10000\\&\approx\$259.80\end{aligned}$$

Therefore, she has enough and is $\$259.80$ over the estimated cost.
